column1: # BundleDock shared shell shortcuts: one table for bash, zsh, fish and Nushell.
# Format: name<TAB>command. Names use [a-z0-9] only so every shell accepts them.
# Commands are plain words; {branch} is the current Git branch (fails on a
# detached HEAD) and {default} is the default branch (origin/HEAD, else main,
# else master). Extra arguments typed after a shortcut are appended.
# Git names follow jhillyerd/plugin-git (MIT, see licenses/shell-layer). The set
# is curated: no --no-verify, git-svn, git-flow or forge-specific entries and no
# The listing family (ll, la, lla, lt, ltr, l1, ltree, llg) runs lsd, which the
# toolbox ships (bundles/toolbox/packages.txt); a test keeps every command's
# first word a base command or a shipped tool. It is read-only: it only reads
# directories and never writes, deletes or changes anything. Stock `ls` is left
# untouched and never aliased: in Nushell `ls` is a built-in that returns a
# table pipelines depend on, an alias would replace it for the whole session,
# and scripts and muscle memory expect the real ls everywhere. Parse rejects any
# shortcut named like a Nushell built-in. Flags are the ones documented for
# --group-dirs <first>. They come from documentation and were not measured here.
# `ltree` is the tree view (lt already means "long, sorted by modification time"; the direction of lsd's -t is from its documentation and has not been run here); `llg` is the
# long listing with directories grouped first.
